paper_title: Bridge the Points: Graph-based Few-shot Segment Anything Semantically
notes: Official code available (NeurIPS 2024 Spotlight). Reference-guided FSS using support images. Positive-Negative Alignment module selects point prompts for SAM via graph analysis and Point-Mask Clustering. Built for natural-image FSS (Pascal-5i/COCO-20i/LVIS-92i). Interface differs from our DINOv2-matching + SAM-B reference-resampling protocol; needs adaptation to medical MoNuSAC/GlaS data and our reference-resampling subsets. No separate trained weights; relies on frozen SAM + DINOv2.

paper_title: SynPo: Boosting Training-Free Few-Shot Medical Segmentation via High-Quality Negative Prompts
code_url: https://liu-yufei.github.io/synpo-project-page/ (project page only; no public code repo confirmed at audit time)
notes: MICCAI 2025 Early Accept. Training-free few-shot medical segmentation. Confidence Map Synergy Module combines DINOv2 and SAM-ViT features; selects positive (top-k) and negative (Gaussian + K-means) point prompts. Reports on Synapse-CT and CHAOS-MRI. Stack aligns closely with ours (DINOv2 + SAM medical). No public GitHub repository confirmed at audit time; project page links only to arXiv. Tier 3 until code is released. Concept comparison only.

paper_title: ProSAM: Enhancing the Robustness of SAM-based Visual Reference Segmentation with Probabilistic Prompts
notes: arXiv:2506.21835 (June 2025) by Bosch Research. Directly addresses instability in SAM-based visual reference segmentation - highly relevant to our work. Learns a variational prompt encoder to predict multivariate prompt distributions avoiding unstable prompt regions. Reports on Pascal-5i and COCO-20i. No public code or weights found in paper or web searches at audit time. Tier 3: concept comparison only. Cannot reproduce without code.

paper_title: MAUP: Training-free Multi-center Adaptive Uncertainty-aware Prompting for Cross-domain Few-shot Medical Image Segmentation
notes: MICCAI 2025. Official code available. Training-free cross-domain few-shot medical segmentation. Generates multi-center prompts via K-means clustering and selects uncertainty-aware prompts with dynamic optimization. Targets abdominal CT/MRI. Interface is cross-domain FSS (source/target domain) which differs from our within-dataset reference-resampling; needs adaptation to map reference images to multi-center prompt generation. Strong reproduction candidate.

paper_title: SAMIX: Reinforcing SAM2 with Semantic Adapter and Reference Selecting Policy for Mix-Supervised Segmentation
weights_url: requires trained SA-SAM2 adapter + SPNet weights
notes: CVPR 2026. Code referenced. Uses SAM2 with a semantic adapter (SA-SAM2) and a Selecting Policy Network (SPNet) trained via RL to auto-regressively retrieve reference samples. Reference selection is conceptually relevant BUT the method is mix-supervised pseudo-label generation requiring RL training of SPNet and SAM2 adaptation. Does not fit our frozen matcher + segmenter test-time reference-resampling protocol. Datasets: PASCAL VOC 2012 Cityscapes camouflaged polyp. Tier 4: not applicable to current task without fundamental redesign.

paper_title: AlignSAM: Aligning Segment Anything Model to Open Context via Reinforcement Learning
weights_url: requires trained RL actor/critic policy weights
notes: CVPR 2024. Official code available. RL-based automatic prompting: an agent iteratively recommends prompt positions to SAM with a semantic recalibration module. NOT reference-guided - it adapts SAM to open-context tasks (saliency/shadow/glass-like) via RL without using reference images. Does not fit our reference-resampling protocol. Tier 4: method not applicable to the reference-guided instability benchmark task.

paper_title: Attack for Defense: Adversarial Agents for Point Prompt Optimization Empowering Segment Anything Model
notes: CVPR 2026. Code available at github.com/L-AILab/PPD. Adversarial RL framework: attacker agent activates prompts that degrade SAM performance; defender agent suppresses them. Plug-and-play point prompt refinement. NOT reference-guided - it optimizes point prompt sets via trained DQN agents without using reference images. Requires trained attacker/defender networks. Tier 4: not applicable to our reference-resampling protocol which uses frozen models and reference images.
